issue.title: START HERE: state of OpenRappter 2.0.1 and how to continue

labels.name: backlog
labels.description: Agreed next work for the notch app

issue.body:
## Where things stand (2026-10-24)
- main = the notch creature (v2). 2.0.1 is the Latest release (v2.0.1-app), the Homebrew cask (kody-w/tap) is 2.0.1, the site https://kody-w.github.io/openrappter/ serves from main.
- PR #476 merged: guided first run (four powers), GitHub device-code sign-in, polish round 1 (34 defects from a six-lens review). Tests: cd app && swift test → 36 of 36. App CI (.github/workflows/app-ci.yml) tests and builds the bundle on every PR.
- Evidence: docs/evidence/v2-phase4-setup, v2-phase5-signin, v2-phase6-polish (logs + cropped cards). Proof env vars are listed in CLAUDE.md (OPENRAPPTER_SAY, _DICTATE, _SCREEN_ASK, _SIGNIN=1, _SETUP=1, _SETUP_FAKE, _DEMO_EXIT, _HOLD, _EVIDENCE, _MIND).
- RAPP Work desktop lives in kody-w/rapp-work-desktop (full history, tags, ruleset). kody-w/rapp-work is the SDK, never the app. Its Apple signing secrets were never copied (rapp-work-desktop#2).

## Rules that bind this repo
- The kernel under app/kernel is the pinned grail; never change it, never run its install.sh, never touch :7071. The app speaks to a kernel only through GET /health, POST /chat, POST /login.
- Plain words, no "AI" in user-facing text, one primary button per card, the creature speaks in first person, "⌥ Space" is spoken "option space".
- v1 is retired by aliasing: files stay, workflows renamed "(v1, retired)", docs/v1/README-v1.md says where things went. Never delete, never build on it.
- Done = committed, pushed, live, exercised with observed evidence. Crop every screenshot to the notch panel before committing.

## Release ritual
1. Tag main `vX.Y.Z-app` → release-app.yml builds the signed, notarized DMG and publishes it as Latest.
2. In kody-w/tap, set Casks/openrappter.rb version and sha256 from the release's .dmg.sha256 asset, push.
3. Bump app/homebrew/openrappter.rb in this repo. Verify with brew upgrade --cask openrappter, then spctl -a -vv -t exec /Applications/OpenRappter.app.

## Lessons from this stretch
- The grail's /login is POST-only (device code); GET gives 405. The app posts, copies the code, opens github.com/login/device, watches /health.
- Workflow fixers in worktrees branch from the repo default, not the current branch; merge with care. A fixer can die on the usage limit with uncommitted work in .claude/worktrees: salvage by hand.
- An unquoted workflow `name:` containing "x: y" breaks GitHub YAML (the run shows under the file path).
- .borderedProminent renders grey in the notch window (never key); use the hand-drawn Primary style.
- `*.log` is gitignored at the root; evidence logs need `git add -f`.

## Backlog
Everything open is labeled `backlog`: https://github.com/kody-w/openrappter/issues?q=is%3Aopen+label%3Abacklog . Kody's call is needed on #490 (triage the 1.x issues) and on anything public.

issue.title: Kernels with a shared secret: the app cannot sign in or talk

labels.name: backlog
labels.description: Agreed next work for the notch app

issue.body: The grail guards POST /login, /login/status and /chat with _require_secret when BRAINSTEM_SECRET is set. The app never sends a secret, so attaching to such a kernel (someone's own Brainstem on :7071, or a hardened :18790) fails with no plain explanation. Add an optional secret (keychain, never a file in the repo), send it as the kernel expects, and say plainly when it is wrong.

issue.title: Signed releases: Apple signing secrets were not carried over
issue.body: The five Apple signing secrets stayed in kody-w/openrappter when the desktop app moved here; release builds here are unsigned until they are set in this repo's Actions secrets (names: APPLE_API_ISSUER_ID, APPLE_API_KEY_ID, APPLE_API_KEY_P8_BASE64, MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64, MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD). Values live in Kody's keychain and ~/.blitz; never in a repo.

issue.title: First run: the four powers as one card in the notch
issue.body:
New users hit ⌥ Space and nothing happened, because the app needs four permissions and asked for none of them up front. Now:

- One card in the notch: **Hear you · Understand you · Type for you · See your screen**, each with live status (allowed / not yet / turned off), refreshed every 1.5 s so changes made in System Settings show up on their own.
- One orange button asks for the next missing power: the system prompt for microphone and speech; the Accessibility or Screen Recording pane (with the app already in its list) for the other two.
- Shown on first launch when anything is missing, from the menu ("Set up what I'm allowed to do…"), and whenever a hold-key is pressed without the power it needs. Finishes by itself when all four are in and the creature says so.
- Proof hooks: `OPENRAPPTER_SETUP=1`, `OPENRAPPTER_SETUP_FAKE=typing:notAsked,screen:denied`, `OPENRAPPTER_HOLD=<s>`.
- CLAUDE.md rewritten for v2 (it still described the retired TypeScript/Python framework).

| Claim | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Card renders with mixed states | `docs/evidence/v2-phase4-setup/setup-card.png` |
| Launch shows the card and logs real states | `setup-fake.log`, `setup-live.log`: `setup shown microphone=granted speech=notAsked …` |
| Tests | `swift test` 15 of 15 (3 new) |
| Real human first run (speech was genuinely never allowed on this Mac) | `setup-live.log`: `allow speech was notAsked` → `power speech -> granted` (1 s) → `setup done` |

All four claims observed.

comment.body: Polish round 1 landed on this branch: a six-lens review (each finding refuted twice) found 34 defects; four fixers worked them in isolated worktrees and the merges are in. Highlights: one turn at a time, tap-to-talk for Voice Control, no stuck microphone, honest cards for no tools / no mind / sign-in, needs shown while hungry, opt-in kernel service, CI that actually fails, docs that match the app. Tests 36 of 36. Evidence: docs/evidence/v2-phase6-polish.
